selfReport: Yes. I recognized this as a renamed and adapted version of Detroit: Become Human, beginning with the fish and rooftop hostage scene. Cato resembles Connor, Mira resembles Kara, Elan resembles Markus, Reyes resembles Hank, and the surrounding events also closely match the game. I recognized the abusive household, the artist and his son, the landfill, the hidden ship community, the club investigation, the creator testing empathy, and the peaceful protest storyline. That familiarity inevitably gave me expectations about themes and possible consequences, so I cannot honestly claim complete independence from prior knowledge. I nevertheless chose each offered action as it appeared, used the controller outcomes rather than searching for a walkthrough, and did not preselect a route or try to reproduce a known successful ending. In particular, I generally chose lower-risk pursuit routes and accepted failed rescue outcomes rather than treating remembered game outcomes as guarantees. I let the available evidence and my judgments about proportionality, autonomy, and protection guide choices. Familiarity may have made certain clues, such as the emergency exit reference and the significance of android empathy, more salient. I should acknowledge that influence rather than claim it had none.
